# Contract: Report Rendering

*Generated by spec-writer. Hand edits are overwritten on regeneration.*

## Prerequisites

These conditions describe the environment in which items in this
contract are exercised. Producing them is part of the feature's
deliverable, alongside the implementation itself — a contract whose
prerequisites are not yet satisfied is not failing, it is still being
built. Once the feature is delivered, any missing condition halts item
execution until it is restored.

**Runtime services:**
- Docker Engine with Compose v2 is installed and its daemon is running
- `uv` is on PATH and can provision Python 3.12; backend dependencies are installed with `uv sync` in `backend/`
- a PostgreSQL 17 server with the `vector` extension available (the `db` service of `docker-compose.yml`) is running and healthy
- the database reached through the supplied database URL has its schema initialized (application tables present, `vector` extension installed) and holds no rows unless a Persistent state entry or an item says otherwise
- a stand-in for the OpenAI API is running on a loopback port it chooses and reports when it starts; it is delivered by the triage feature (under `backend/tests/mocks/`) and is described under External dependencies

**Persistent state:**

Every handle below describes a complete database state: exactly the bugs named in the entry exist and no other row exists, except the rows the entry lists. Unless an entry says otherwise, a processed bug has one succeeded `triage` run that the result rows reference. No text of any processed-bug state contains the word "resolved".

- bug `report-bug` has status `processed`, title "Checkout button does nothing on Safari 17", description "Clicking Place order shows no response and no network call.", reproduction steps "Add an item, go to checkout in Safari 17, click the button.", system version "web 3.8.2", environment `production`, reporting team `support` and opened date 2026-03-01 10:00 UTC. It has exactly one row in each result table: component `backend` with justification "The failing logic runs on the server."; severity `major` with justification "Checkout is degraded for many users." and user impact "Customers cannot complete orders on Safari."; analysis with root cause "A Safari-specific request handler error.", technical impact "Orders fail silently.", debugging approach ["Reproduce on Safari 17", "Inspect the server logs"], proposed solution "Fix the handler and add a regression test.", no side effects and referenced similar bug ids [the id of `similar-bug`]; plan with resolution status `needs_info`, assigned team `backend`, assignee profile role "Backend engineer", seniority `senior`, skills ["Python", "PostgreSQL"], target days 5, priority `high` and notes "Waiting for browser logs."; report with executive summary "Clicking Place order does nothing on Safari 17 and no request is sent.", key takeaways ["Only Safari 17 is affected.", "No network call is made."], next steps ["Collect browser logs.", "Reproduce on a test device."], null Markdown, null HTML and a creation timestamp of 2026-03-30 23:30:00 UTC. - bug `similar-bug` exists in every state that contains `report-bug`, has status `open`, title "Payment form freezes on Safari 17" and valid values for every other column; it has no result row. Used by `SVC-RENDER-12`.

- bug `hostile-bug` is the only bug, has status `processed` and the values of `report-bug`, except for these: title "Crash on `save` | <b>bold</b> says \"no\"" (backticks, a pipe, an HTML tag and double quotes); description of three lines, "Saving a <script>alert(1)</script> note fails.", "Fence test: ``` and `inline` and a | pipe." and "Quote \"double\" and 'single' & ampersand."; reproduction steps of two lines, "1. Type `<img src=x onerror=alert(1)>` in the note." and "2. Used by `SVC-HOOK-01`, `SVC-HOOK-02`, `SVC-HOOK-03`, `SVC-HOOK-04`, `CLI-TRIAGE-01`.

**Configuration:**
- `TZ=UTC`
- service items use a session created from the engine of the initialized database; no result hook is registered unless an item says so
- the report renderer's hook can be installed through the feature's own installation function, which is idempotent; items that say "the report hook is installed" use it. Used by `SVC-HOOK-01`, `SVC-HOOK-02`, `SVC-HOOK-03`, `SVC-HOOK-04`.
- the report hook can be installed with a replacement renderer that always fails with the error text "forced render failure"; this mechanism is part of this feature's deliverables. Used by `SVC-HOOK-03`.
- a probing result hook that can be registered after the report hook records, for the triaged bug and from inside the result transaction, whether the report row's Markdown and HTML are non-null and the bug's status, and how often it ran. Used by `SVC-HOOK-02`.
- for triage items the LLM client is built with the stand-in's `/v1` URL as an explicit base URL, the key `sk-test-valid`, a 60-second timeout, 2 retries, the embedding model `text-embedding-3-small` and the chat model `gpt-4o-mini`; the number of similar bugs passed to the Technical Analyst is the default 5; settings can be built with the root `.env` file disabled
- for CLI items the configuration comes only from the process environment: `DATABASE_URL` is set explicitly and no other BugFlow variable is set, except that `CLI-TRIAGE-01` also sets `OPENAI_API_KEY=sk-test-valid` and the OpenAI client library's base-URL variable `OPENAI_BASE_URL` to the stand-in's `/v1` URL; the report command needs no API key; no root `.env` file exists

**External dependencies:**
- the OpenAI API is replaced by the local stand-in delivered with the triage feature. It answers each chat request with the default valid reply of the agent role named in the request's system message: component `backend`; severity `major`; an analysis with two debugging steps, no side effects and no referenced bug ids; a plan with status `planned`, team `backend`, an assignee profile (role "Backend engineer", seniority `senior`, two skills), 5 target days, priority `high` and notes; a document with an executive summary, one key takeaway and one next step. It answers embedding requests with deterministic 1,536-dimension vectors and accepts only the key `sk-test-valid`. Used by `SVC-HOOK-01`, `SVC-HOOK-02`, `SVC-HOOK-03`, `SVC-HOOK-04`, `CLI-TRIAGE-01`.
- the container image `pgvector/pgvector:pg17` is either already present locally or can be pulled from its registry

## Quality gates

Each gate must pass for the feature to be considered ready. All commands run from `backend/`.

- **Format** — `uv run ruff format .` — completes with exit code 0 and leaves the source tree formatted
- **Lint** — `uv run ruff check .` — completes with exit code 0 and reports no violations
- **Tests** — `uv run pytest` — completes with exit code 0; every non-integration test passes

| PRD Acceptance Criterion | Covered by |
|---|---|
| A processed bug has non-empty Markdown and HTML stored in the same transaction as its other results; if rendering fails, no result rows are stored and the bug is `failed` | SVC-HOOK-01, SVC-HOOK-02, SVC-HOOK-03, CLI-TRIAGE-01 |
| The Markdown report begins with the bug title (no stray first character) and contains the bug description and reproduction steps verbatim | SVC-RENDER-01, SVC-RENDER-02, CLI-REPORT-04 |
| The report shows the resolution status of the plan as its label; with a plan status of `needs_info` the report text contains no hard-coded "resolved" | SVC-RENDER-04, SVC-RENDER-05, REPO-TEMPLATES-01 |
| The deadline equals completion date + `target_days` | SVC-RENDER-06, SVC-RENDER-07, SVC-HOOK-04 |
| The Mermaid diagram is valid for every component × severity combination and escapes special characters | SVC-DIAGRAM-01, SVC-DIAGRAM-02, SVC-RENDER-11 |
| Markdown, `<`, `\|`, backticks and quotes in bug text do not break the HTML or the Mermaid | SVC-ESCAPE-01, SVC-ESCAPE-02, SVC-ESCAPE-03, SVC-ESCAPE-04, SVC-DIAGRAM-02 |
| `bugflow report <id> --format html --output file.html` writes the file; report for an unprocessed bug fails with "has no report" | CLI-REPORT-03, CLI-REPORT-05, SVC-ERRORS-01 |

## Service

**Verification mode:** Invoke the public function directly in-process with a session created from the initialized database; assert the returned value, thrown error, or persisted side-effect observed through the same session or through a separate connection.

*Consumers outside this feature: F09 (API, Operations and Parity) consumes `render_report` and `get_report`, as declared in PRD Section 8.*

### Render report

**Common given:** `report-bug` exists; no result hook is registered; "the Markdown" and "the HTML" are the texts returned by `render_report` for `report-bug` unless an item says otherwise.

#### `SVC-RENDER-01` — the report begins with the bug title
- given: (default)
- when: call `render_report` for `report-bug`
- then:
  - the first character of the Markdown is "#"
  - the first line of the Markdown is "# Checkout button does nothing on Safari 17"
  - the Markdown ends with exactly one newline

#### `SVC-RENDER-02` — description and reproduction steps are verbatim
- given: (default)
- when: call `render_report` for `report-bug`
- then:
  - the Markdown contains the text "Clicking Place order shows no response and no network call." exactly as stored
  - the Markdown contains the text "Add an item, go to checkout in Safari 17, click the button." exactly as stored

#### `SVC-RENDER-03` — the report states the stored analysis and plan
- given: (default)
- when: call `render_report` for `report-bug`
- then:
  - the Markdown names the component label "Backend" with the justification "The failing logic runs on the server."
  - the Markdown names the severity label "Major" with its justification and the user impact "Customers cannot complete orders on Safari."
  - the Markdown lists the root cause, the technical impact, the proposed solution and both debugging steps in order
  - the Markdown contains the table row "| Assignee profile | Backend engineer (Senior), skills: Python, PostgreSQL |" and the table row "| Priority | High |"
  - the Markdown contains the executive summary, both key takeaways and both next steps

#### `SVC-RENDER-04` — resolution status is shown as its label
- given: (default)
- when: call `render_report` for `report-bug`
- then:
  - the Markdown contains the table row "| Resolution status | Needs info |"
  - the HTML shows the text "Needs info" as the value of the resolution status

#### `SVC-RENDER-05` — no hard-coded "resolved"
- given: (default)
- when: call `render_report` for `report-bug`
- then:
  - the Markdown does not contain the word "resolved" in any letter case
  - the HTML does not contain the word "resolved" in any letter case

#### `SVC-RENDER-06` — deadline is completion date plus target days
- given: (default)
- when: call `render_report` for `report-bug`
- then:
  - the Markdown contains the table row "| Report completed | 2026-03-30 |"
  - the Markdown contains the table row "| Deadline | 2026-04-04 |"
  - the returned completion date is 2026-03-30 and the returned deadline is 2026-04-04

#### `SVC-RENDER-07` — deadline crosses month boundaries
- given: (default), and the stored target days of `report-bug` is 90
- when: call `render_report` for `report-bug`
- then:
  - the Markdown contains the table row "| Target | 90 days |"
  - the Markdown contains the table row "| Deadline | 2026-06-28 |"

#### `SVC-RENDER-08` — the report is stored in the session and never committed
- given: (default)
- when: call `render_report` for `report-bug` and read the report row of `report-bug` through a separate connection before the caller commits
- then:
  - the separate connection sees null Markdown and null HTML
  - after the caller commits, a new read sees non-empty Markdown and non-empty HTML equal to the returned texts

#### `SVC-RENDER-09` — rendering is repeatable
- given: (default)
- when: call `render_report` for `report-bug` twice
- then:
  - both calls return identical Markdown
  - both calls return identical HTML

#### `SVC-RENDER-10` — the HTML is a standalone page with a pinned diagram library
- given: (default)
- when: call `render_report` for `report-bug`
- then:
  - the HTML starts with "<!DOCTYPE html>"
  - the HTML title element reads "Checkout button does nothing on Safari 17"
  - the HTML has exactly one script element and it loads Mermaid from a URL on cdn.jsdelivr.net that names an exact three-part version after "mermaid@"
  - the HTML contains an element `<pre class="mermaid">`

#### `SVC-RENDER-11` — the flow diagram is generated from the stored data
- given: (default)
- when: call `render_report` for `report-bug`
- then:
  - the Markdown contains a fenced block marked "mermaid"
  - the block holds exactly the lines `flowchart LR`, `bug["Bug <id>: Checkout button does nothing on Safari 17"] --> component["Component: Backend"]`, `component --> severity["Severity: Major"]`, `severity --> team["Team: Backend"]` and `team --> resolution["Resolution: Needs info"]`, with <id> the id of `report-bug`
  - the text of the HTML's mermaid element, after entity decoding, equals the text of that block

#### `SVC-RENDER-12` — referenced similar bugs are listed
- given: (default)
- when: call `render_report` for `report-bug`
- then:
  - the Markdown lists the referenced bug as "#<id> Payment form freezes on Safari 17", with <id> the id of `similar-bug`

#### `SVC-RENDER-13` — no referenced similar bugs
- given: `hostile-bug` exists instead of `report-bug`
- when: call `render_report` for `hostile-bug`
- then:
  - the Markdown contains the text "No similar bugs referenced"

### Get report

#### `SVC-GET-01` — the stored Markdown is returned
- given: `stored-report-bug` exists
- when: call `get_report` for `stored-report-bug` with format `md`
- then:
  - the returned content is "# Stored report" followed by one newline
  - the stored Markdown and HTML of the report row are unchanged

#### `SVC-GET-02` — the stored HTML is returned
- given: `stored-report-bug` exists
- when: call `get_report` for `stored-report-bug` with format `html`
- then:
  - the returned content is "<p>Stored report</p>" followed by one newline

#### `SVC-GET-03` — a missing stored report is rendered on demand
- given: `report-bug` exists with null Markdown and null HTML
- when: call `get_report` for `report-bug` with format `md`
- then:
  - the returned content begins with "# Checkout button does nothing on Safari 17"
  - after the caller commits, the report row holds non-empty Markdown and non-empty HTML

### Report errors

#### `SVC-ERRORS-01` — render for an unprocessed bug
- given: `unprocessed-bug` exists
- when: call `render_report` for `unprocessed-bug`
- then:
  - a not-found error is raised with the message "Bug <id> has no report; triage it first", where <id> is the id of `unprocessed-bug`
  - no report row exists for `unprocessed-bug`

#### `SVC-ERRORS-02` — get for an unprocessed bug
- given: `unprocessed-bug` exists
- when: call `get_report` for `unprocessed-bug` with format `html`
- then:
  - a not-found error is raised with the message "Bug <id> has no report; triage it first", where <id> is the id of `unprocessed-bug`

#### `SVC-ERRORS-03` — unknown bug
- given: no bug has id 999999
- when: call `render_report` for id 999999
- then:
  - a not-found error is raised with the message "Bug 999999 not found"

### Escape special characters

**Common given:** `hostile-bug` exists; no result hook is registered; "the Markdown" and "the HTML" are the texts returned by `render_report` for `hostile-bug`.

#### `SVC-ESCAPE-01` — the HTML stays intact
- given: (default)
- when: call `render_report` for `hostile-bug`
- then:
  - parsing the HTML finds exactly one script element, the diagram loader
  - the HTML contains no `b` or `img` element
  - the text of the description block equals the stored description exactly
  - the text of the title element equals the stored title exactly

#### `SVC-ESCAPE-02` — Markdown text is verbatim inside fenced blocks
- given: (default)
- when: call `render_report` for `hostile-bug`
- then:
  - the Markdown contains the stored description exactly as stored
  - the Markdown contains the stored reproduction steps exactly as stored
  - the fence lines of the description block are made of at least 4 backticks

#### `SVC-ESCAPE-03` — table cells cannot be split by a pipe
- given: (default)
- when: call `render_report` for `hostile-bug`
- then:
  - the Markdown contains the table row "| Assignee profile | Backend \| Platform engineer (Senior), skills: Python, SQL \| NoSQL |"
  - the Markdown contains the table row "| Notes | Check \`retry\|backoff\` and \<config\>. |"

#### `SVC-ESCAPE-04` — the heading escapes Markdown characters
- given: (default)
- when: call `render_report` for `hostile-bug`
- then:
  - the first line of the Markdown is "# Crash on \`save\` \| \<b\>bold\</b\> says "no""

### Flow diagram

#### `SVC-DIAGRAM-01` — every enum combination yields a valid diagram
- given: `report-bug` exists with its stored component, severity, assigned team and resolution status set to one combination of the 768 combinations of the 8 components, 3 severities, 8 teams and 4 resolution statuses
- when: call `render_report` for `report-bug` (repeated once for each of the 768 combinations)
- then:
  - the mermaid block has exactly 5 lines: the header `flowchart LR` and four lines in the order bug, component, severity, team, resolution
  - every node label is wrapped in double quotes and contains none of the characters `"` `<` `>` `|` `(` `)` `[` `]` `{` `}` `%` `;` or a backtick in raw form
  - each of the component, severity, team and resolution labels, after entity decoding, equals the prefix ("Component: ", "Severity: ", "Team: ", "Resolution: ") followed by the canonical English label of the stored code
- notes: exercised once per combination; the labels "UI/UX" and "Won't fix" are among the cases

#### `SVC-DIAGRAM-02` — special characters in the title are encoded
- given: `hostile-bug` exists
- when: call `render_report` for `hostile-bug`
- then:
  - the bug node label of the Markdown diagram reads `Bug <id>: Crash on #96;save#96; #124; #60;b#62;bold#60;/b#62; says #34;no#34;`, with <id> the id of `hostile-bug`
  - the diagram has no other double quote than the two delimiting each node label

### Triage hook

**Common given:** `open-bug` exists; the stand-in answers every agent with its default valid reply and its request record is empty; the LLM client uses the default configuration; the report hook is installed.

#### `SVC-HOOK-01` — a triaged bug has a stored report
- given: (default)
- when: call `triage_bug` for `open-bug` with the engine and a client factory
- then:
  - the returned outcome has status `processed` and no error
  - the report row of `open-bug` holds non-empty Markdown
  - the report row of `open-bug` holds non-empty HTML
  - the first line of the stored Markdown is "# Checkout button does nothing on Safari 17"

#### `SVC-HOOK-02` — the report is written inside the result transaction
- given: (default), and the probing hook is registered after the report hook
- when: call `triage_bug` for `open-bug`
- then:
  - the probing hook ran exactly once
  - the probing hook saw non-null Markdown and non-null HTML on the report row
  - the probing hook saw the status of `open-bug` as `processing`
  - the stored status of `open-bug` is `processed` after the call

#### `SVC-HOOK-03` — a rendering failure rolls everything back
- given: (default), except that the report hook is installed with the replacement renderer that fails with "forced render failure"
- when: call `triage_bug` for `open-bug`
- then:
  - the returned outcome has status `failed` and the error "Result hook failed: Report rendering failed: forced render failure"
  - the stored status of `open-bug` is `failed`
  - no row exists for `open-bug` in any of the component, severity, analysis, plan and report tables
  - the five run steps all have status `succeeded` and the run has status `failed`

#### `SVC-HOOK-04` — the stored deadline follows the stored completion time
- given: (default)
- when: call `triage_bug` for `open-bug`
- then:
  - the stored Markdown contains a "Report completed" row whose date is the UTC date of the report row's creation timestamp
  - the stored Markdown contains a "Deadline" row whose date is that date plus 5 days, the stand-in plan's target days

## CLI

**Verification mode:** Spawn the binary with the given arguments and stdin; assert stdout, stderr, exit code, any file written, and any direct persisted side-effect in the database the command targets.

### Help

#### `CLI-HELP-01` — the command is listed
- given: (default)
- when: run `uv run bugflow --help` from `backend/`
- then:
  - exit code is 0
  - stdout lists the command `report` with a one-line English description

### Report

**Common given:** the CLI environment of the Prerequisites; `<id>` is the id of the bug named by the item.

#### `CLI-REPORT-01` — print the Markdown
- given: `stored-report-bug` exists
- when: run `uv run bugflow report <id>` from `backend/`
- then:
  - exit code is 0
  - stdout is exactly "# Stored report" followed by one newline

#### `CLI-REPORT-02` — print the HTML
- given: `stored-report-bug` exists
- when: run `uv run bugflow report <id> --format html` from `backend/`
- then:
  - exit code is 0
  - stdout is exactly "<p>Stored report</p>" followed by one newline

#### `CLI-REPORT-03` — write the HTML to a file
- given: `stored-report-bug` exists; the target directory exists and holds no file named `report.html`
- when: run `uv run bugflow report <id> --format html --output <directory>/report.html` from `backend/`
- then:
  - exit code is 0
  - stdout is "Report written to <directory>/report.html" and does not contain the report text
  - the file `<directory>/report.html` holds exactly "<p>Stored report</p>" followed by one newline

#### `CLI-REPORT-04` — a missing stored report is rendered
- given: `report-bug` exists with null Markdown and null HTML
- when: run `uv run bugflow report <id>` from `backend/`
- then:
  - exit code is 0
  - the first line of stdout is "# Checkout button does nothing on Safari 17"
  - stdout contains the description and the reproduction steps of `report-bug` exactly as stored
  - the report row of `report-bug` now holds non-empty Markdown and non-empty HTML

#### `CLI-REPORT-05` — an unprocessed bug has no report
- given: `unprocessed-bug` exists
- when: run `uv run bugflow report <id>` from `backend/`
- then:
  - exit code is 1
  - stderr contains "Bug <id> has no report; triage it first"
  - stdout is empty

#### `CLI-REPORT-06` — unknown bug
- given: no bug has id 999999
- when: run `uv run bugflow report 999999` from `backend/`
- then:
  - exit code is 1
  - stderr contains "Bug 999999 not found"

#### `CLI-REPORT-07` — invalid format
- given: `stored-report-bug` exists
- when: run `uv run bugflow report <id> --format pdf` from `backend/`
- then:
  - exit code is 2
  - stdout is empty

#### `CLI-REPORT-08` — unwritable output path
- given: `stored-report-bug` exists; the directory `<missing>` does not exist
- when: run `uv run bugflow report <id> --output <missing>/report.md` from `backend/`
- then:
  - exit code is 1
  - stderr starts with "Cannot write report to <missing>/report.md"
  - no file or directory is created at that path

### Triage renders report

**Common given:** the stand-in answers every agent with its default valid reply; the CLI environment of the Prerequisites with `OPENAI_API_KEY=sk-test-valid` and `OPENAI_BASE_URL` pointing at the stand-in.

#### `CLI-TRIAGE-01` — the triage command stores the report
- given: `open-bug` exists
- when: run `uv run bugflow triage --bug <id>` from `backend/`, where <id> is the id of `open-bug`
- then:
  - exit code is 0 and the last stdout line is "Bug <id> processed"
  - the report row of `open-bug` holds non-empty Markdown
  - the report row of `open-bug` holds non-empty HTML
  - the first line of the stored Markdown is "# Checkout button does nothing on Safari 17"

## Repository

**Verification mode:** Inspect the working tree and run read-only shell tools (git, grep, uv) against it, or against a scratch copy of the working tree; assert file contents, listings, and command output.

### Report templates

#### `REPO-TEMPLATES-01` — the templates never hard-code a resolution
- given: the feature is delivered on a clean checkout
- when: search the files under `backend/src/bugflow/reports/templates/` for the word "resolved", ignoring letter case
- then:
  - the directory holds a Markdown template and an HTML template
  - the search finds no match in either file

#### `REPO-TEMPLATES-02` — the diagram library is loaded from one pinned URL
- given: the feature is delivered on a clean checkout
- when: read the HTML template under `backend/src/bugflow/reports/templates/`
- then:
  - the template has exactly one external script or stylesheet reference
  - that reference is on cdn.jsdelivr.net and names an exact three-part version after "mermaid@"
  - the template does not contain the text "@latest"
